report.tagline: An online marketplace where millions of small sellers sell handmade, vintage and unique items to buyers around the world.
report.simpleSummary: Etsy is a website and app where you can buy things you will not find in a normal shop: a hand-stamped necklace with your mum's name, a vintage 1970s lamp, or a printable wedding invite. The sellers are mostly individuals and tiny businesses working from home. Etsy does not hold stock; it runs the marketplace and takes a cut of each sale. Its big fight is keeping cheap mass-made goods from crowding out real makers.

overview.whatItDoes: Etsy connects buyers with independent sellers of handmade, vintage, craft supplies and personalised goods. Sellers set up shops, list items and handle making and shipping. Etsy provides search, payments, buyer protection, ads and shipping labels, and takes fees on each sale. It is run by CEO Kruti Patel Goyal since 2026.
howItWorks: A seller opens a shop, pays $0.20 to list each item for four months, and writes titles, tags and photos.
Buyers search, browse gift guides or get personalised recommendations in the app.
When something sells, Etsy takes a 6.5% transaction fee plus payment processing fees (about 3% plus a small fixed fee in the US, a bit higher in the UK).
Sellers can pay for Etsy Ads to rank higher in search, and Etsy runs Offsite Ads on Google and social media, charging 12% to 15% of the sale if it brings a buyer.
Etsy's search now weighs quality and the likely post-purchase experience, not just whether a listing will sell.
Etsy's Purchase Protection refunds buyers if an order does not arrive or is not as described.
overview.valueProposition: For buyers: unique, personal and handmade items you cannot find elsewhere. For sellers: access to about 88 million buyers without building their own website.

businessModel.summary: Etsy makes money from sellers, not buyers. It charges listing fees, a cut of each sale, payment processing fees, and sells ads and shipping labels. Its take rate, the share of each sale Etsy keeps, is about 26%.

revenueStreams.detail: $0.20 listing fee, 6.5% transaction fee and payment processing fees. $468 million in Q3 2026.
Etsy Ads (sellers pay per click) and Offsite Ads (12% to 15% of sales Etsy brings from outside).
Margin on shipping labels and other seller tools. Services revenue was $224 million in Q3 2026.
Optional seller subscription with extra tools for about $10 a month.

businessModel.pricing: Listing fee $0.20 per item. Transaction fee 6.5% of the total including shipping. Payment processing about 3% + $0.25 in the US (UK about 4% + £0.20). Offsite Ads fee 15% of the sale, or 12% for sellers who made over $10,000 in a year. Shoppers pay nothing extra. Check Etsy's fee page for current rates by country.
costDrivers: Marketing, mainly Google and social ads to bring buyers (about $207 million in Q3 2026)
Engineering for search, recommendations and the app
Trust and safety: removing mass-produced, fake and AI-spam listings
Payment processing costs paid to card networks
Customer support and Purchase Protection refunds
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a $40 personalised necklace with $5 shipping. The seller pays $0.20 to list it, about $2.93 in transaction fees, and about $1.60 in payment processing. If it came through Offsite Ads, the seller pays another $6.75. So Etsy collects about $4.70 to $11.50 on this sale. Etsy's cost of processing the payment is about $1.30, and it spends heavily on marketing to bring buyers back. With a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, Etsy keeps roughly $1.50 to $3.50 of profit on this sale. For the seller, fees take 12% to 25% of the price.

growth.moat: Etsy has a two-sided network effect: 88 million buyers attract 5.8 million sellers, and the huge range of unique items attracts buyers. Its brand means 'handmade and personal', which Amazon Handmade and Temu have not matched. The moat weakens if Etsy fills with mass-made goods that buyers can get cheaper elsewhere.

competitors.name: Amazon Handmade
competitors.positioning: Amazon's handmade section with fast Prime delivery.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Amazon wins on delivery speed; Etsy wins on range of unique and personalised items and on brand.

competitors.name: Temu and Shein
competitors.positioning: Very cheap factory goods shipped from China.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Etsy competes on uniqueness and quality, not price. Copies of Etsy designs on Temu are a threat.

competitors.name: eBay (now owns Depop)
competitors.positioning: Marketplace for used, vintage and collectibles.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Etsy is stronger for handmade and gifting; eBay for collectibles and resale.

competitors.name: Shopify
competitors.positioning: Lets sellers build their own online store.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Shopify gives control and lower fees but no built-in buyers; Etsy brings traffic.

competitors.name: Meesho (India, for comparison)
competitors.positioning: Indian marketplace for small sellers, zero commission, earns from ads and logistics.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Meesho competes on low prices; Etsy charges sellers more and positions on uniqueness.

northStar.metric: Number of buyers who make a repeat purchase within 12 months
northStar.why: Repeat buyers show that Etsy delivered a good item and a good experience. It also measures trust and search quality, and drives GMS without heavy marketing spend.

pmLessons: A marketplace's brand is its supply. If cheap mass-made goods take over, buyers lose the reason to come.
Raising take rate through ads boosts revenue but can push away sellers; watch both sides.
Search ranking is product policy. What you rank shapes what sellers make.
Selling side businesses (Depop, Reverb) to focus on the core is a valid strategy.

interviewQuestions.question: Purchase frequency is falling. How would you fix it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment buyers. Find drop-off reasons. Ideas: occasion reminders, personalisation, gift mode. Metric: purchases per buyer.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you keep Etsy unique as mass-produced items grow?
interviewQuestions.hint: Policy, detection, badges, ranking. Balance seller growth with quality. Guardrail: false removals.

interviewQuestions.question: Etsy wants to raise ad revenue. What are the risks?
interviewQuestions.hint: Seller costs, buyer experience with too many ads. Track take rate and seller churn together.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Etsy with Meesho.
interviewQuestions.hint: Both serve small sellers. Different monetisation (fees vs zero commission), price points, buyers. What can each learn?

interviewQuestions.question: What north star metric would you choose for Etsy?
interviewQuestions.hint: Repeat buyers or GMS from repeat buyers. Explain why GMS alone hides quality problems.
